question: What causes metabolic joint diseases?

options.A: Wear and tear of cartilage from aging
options.B: Autoimmune destruction of the joint lining

explanation: Metabolic joint diseases happen when chemical errors cause substances to build up inside the joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h1)

question: How are metabolic joint diseases different from normal osteoarthritis?

options.A: Metabolic joint diseases never affect joint fluid
options.B: Osteoarthritis involves sudden uric acid crystals
options.C: Metabolic joint diseases come from chemical processing errors
options.D: Osteoarthritis is caused by too much purine

explanation: Osteoarthritis is mostly wear and tear, while metabolic disorders are driven by specific body chemistry problems. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h1)

question: High levels of which substance lead to monosodium urate crystals?
explanation: High amounts of uric acid in the body directly lead to the formation of these crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why do uric acid crystals often form in outer joints like the big toe?

options.A: Cartilage in the toes has no fluid
options.B: Blood does not flow to the toes
options.C: Walking causes too much friction there
options.D: Cooler body temperatures make it easier for crystals to form

explanation: Lower temperatures in joints further from the core make it harder for fluids to hold dissolved substances, causing crystals to drop out. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h2)

question: Pseudogout is a type of crystal disease involving which substance?
explanation: Pseudogout happens when calcium pyrophosphate crystals deposit inside the joint cartilage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h3)

question: A patient with gout has a problem breaking down which substance?
explanation: Uric acid is the leftover product of purine breakdown, so gout is tied to how the body handles purines. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h3)

question: Which type of medication can slow down uric acid removal by the kidneys and trigger gout?
explanation: Many water pills reduce the kidneys' ability to pass out uric acid, raising levels in the blood. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which lifestyle habit plays a major role in causing high uric acid and gout?

options.D: Eating purine-rich foods and drinking alcohol

explanation: Dietary purines turn into uric acid, and alcohol makes it harder for the body to get rid of it. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h4)

question: What are the hard, chalky bumps of crystal deposits under the skin called?
explanation: Tophi are solid lumps of uric acid crystals that form under the skin in long-term gout. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which joint is most commonly affected during a first gout attack?
explanation: The base of the big toe is the classic spot for a first gout flare due to local temperature and body mechanics. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is the best way to confirm a crystal-caused joint disease?

options.B: Drawing joint fluid with a needle for lab analysis

explanation: Testing the fluid taken from the joint directly reveals the presence of crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h6)

question: Under a special microscope, how do uric acid crystals look?
explanation: Microscopic view shows distinct needle-like shapes when checking for gout crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h6)

question: Which drug is commonly given to lower uric acid levels over the long term?
explanation: Allopurinol works by blocking the enzyme that makes uric acid, helping control levels over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why can starting a uric acid-lowering drug sometimes cause a temporary joint flare?

options.A: The medication reacts directly with joint fluid
options.B: The drugs cause sudden kidney failure
options.C: The pills make white blood cells multiply fast
options.D: Shifting uric acid levels shake loose old crystal deposits

explanation: When blood uric acid drops, stored crystals start to dissolve and break off into the joint, causing brief irritation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is a good nursing action to protect a sore joint during an acute gout flare?

options.C: Keep bed sheets lifted off the joint using a cradle

explanation: Even the light weight of bed covers can cause intense pain during an active gout attack. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h8)

question: Why do nurses encourage patients with gout to drink plenty of water?

options.A: To thin out red blood cells
options.B: To help the kidneys pass uric acid and stop stones
options.C: To flush calcium out through the skin
options.D: To stop dehydration from pain meds

explanation: Drinking lots of fluids helps the kidneys clear out uric acid smoothly and lowers the chance of kidney stones. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h8)
